findings.title: Dynamic imports are eagerly started, not lazy
findings.body: Every value is an already-executed import() call in the object literal, so importing appStore immediately initiates loading all ~30 app modules instead of loading only the requested app on first use. This defeats the stated purpose of the PR and keeps the startup/bundle-evaluation cost (and side effects) of every app for any caller that needs just one. The promises should be wrapped in thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with callers invoking them. A related consequence is that a failing optional app creates a rejected promise at import time that may surface as an unhandled rejection even if that app is never used.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race with Promise.all(apiDeletes)
findings.body: The recurring-cancellation branch uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. The async callback suspends at the await, so execution reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (and the success response) before the pushes happen. Previously getCalendar was synchronous and the pushes happened during forEach. Now calendar deleteEvent calls for recurring bookings are typically never awaited and may not even have started when the handler returns, leaving events on external calendars; errors from them are also unhandled.

findings.title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and bypasses try/catch
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is never awaited: forEach ignores the returned promises, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from the async callback. Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before (and regardless of whether) the old calendar/video events are deleted, so failures are silently lost as unhandled rejections and stale events can remain. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

findings.title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and bypasses try/catch
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is never awaited: forEach ignores the returned promises, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from the async callback. Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before (and regardless of whether) the old calendar/video events are deleted, so failures are silently lost as unhandled rejections and stale events can remain. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not await async calendar/video deletions
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` discards the promises returned by the async callback. The mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and webhooks and returns, so the previous calendar/video events may still exist (or fail silently as unhandled rejections) when the user reschedules via the emailed link. Await the deletions, e.g. with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`, before proceeding.
